title: Compactifiable comparison of correspondence six-operation diagrams
statement:
Use the finite coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $c:C\to X\times_kX$ and $\bar c:\bar C\to\bar X\times_k\bar X$ be correspondences of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-trf-correspondence]. Their fixed diagrams [def-trf-fixed-scheme] have objects $X,X\times X,C,F=\operatorname{Fix}(c),s$ and arrows the identities, structure maps $a_Z$, projections $p_i$, $c,c_i$, diagonals $\Delta$, fixed inclusions $i_F$, fixed projections $d$, and $ci_F=\Delta d$; barred symbols denote the corresponding objects and arrows for $\bar c$. Work in the finite-Tor constructible categories with the specified ordinary and exceptional adjunctions of [def-trf-admissibility] and the normalized geometric operation datum of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Derived notation is understood throughout.

A cohomological pre-comparison is data
$$f_Z:D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)\to D^b_{ctf}(\bar Z,A),\quad t_Z:f_ZM\otimes f_ZN\to f_Z(M\otimes N),\quad\alpha_g:\bar g^*f_V\to f_Ug^*,\quad\beta_g:f_Ug^!\to\bar g^!f_V,\quad\iota:f_sA_s\xrightarrow{\sim}A_s$$
for each diagram arrow $g:U\to V$. Put $\omega_Z=Ra_Z^!A_s$ and $D_ZM=R\mathcal Hom(M,\omega_Z)$ [def-trf-dualizing-complex]. Define $\delta_Z:f_Z\omega_Z\to\omega_{\bar Z}$ by $\beta_{a_Z}$ followed by $a_{\bar Z}^!\iota$. Define $r_Z:f_ZR\mathcal Hom(M,N)\to R\mathcal Hom(f_ZM,f_ZN)$ as the transpose of $f_ZR\mathcal Hom(M,N)\otimes f_ZM\xrightarrow{t_Z}f_Z(R\mathcal Hom(M,N)\otimes M)\xrightarrow{f_Z\operatorname{ev}}f_ZN$, and $d_Z:f_ZD_ZM\to D_{\bar Z}f_ZM$ as $r_Z$ followed by postcomposition with $\delta_Z$.

The ordinary mate $\alpha_{g,*}:f_VRg_*\to R\bar g_*f_U$ is defined by transposing $\bar g^*f_VRg_*\xrightarrow{\alpha_g}f_Ug^*Rg_*\xrightarrow{f_U\varepsilon_g}f_U$. The exceptional mate $\beta_{g,!}:R\bar g_!f_U\to f_VRg_!$ is defined by transposing $f_U\xrightarrow{f_U\eta_g}f_Ug^!Rg_!\xrightarrow{\beta_g} \bar g^!f_VRg_!$.

A pre-comparison is compactifiable when it satisfies the following seven requirements. (I) Each $t_Z$ is associative and compatible with signed tensor symmetry. (II) $\iota\circ t_s=\iota\otimes\iota$ on $f_sA_s\otimes f_sA_s$, with the unit identifications inserted. (III) $\alpha_{\operatorname{id}}=\operatorname{id}$ and $\alpha_{hg}=\alpha_g\circ\bar g^*\alpha_h$ under the pullback compositors. (IV) Ordinary comparison respects tensor: $\alpha_g(M\otimes N)\circ\bar g^*t_V=t_U\circ(\alpha_g(M)\otimes\alpha_g(N))$. (V) Each evaluation-defined $d_Z$ is an isomorphism. (VI) If both $g$ and $\bar g$ are proper, then $\alpha_{g,*}$ and $\beta_{g,!}$ are inverse isomorphisms, under $Rg_!=Rg_*$ and $R\bar g_!=R\bar g_*$. (VII) There exist compactifications by open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], $X\subset X^*$, $C\subset C^*$, $c^*:C^*\to X^*\times X^*$ and their barred counterparts, with $X^*,C^*,\bar X^*,\bar C^*$ proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], for which the functors and all comparison maps extend to the compactified fixed diagrams satisfying (I)--(VI); restriction to the open subcorrespondences identifies the extended data with the given data.

A cohomological comparison is a finite composite of compactifiable pre-comparisons. Composition means objectwise composition of the functors, successive tensor maps, and the whiskered composites of $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\iota$. Also write
$$j_Z:A_{\bar Z}\xrightarrow{\sim}a_{\bar Z}^*A_s\xrightarrow{a_{\bar Z}^*(\iota^{-1})}a_{\bar Z}^*f_sA_s\xrightarrow{\alpha_{a_Z}(A_s)}f_Za_Z^*A_s=f_ZA_Z,\qquad h_Z(q)=f_Z(q)\circ j_Z\quad(q:A_Z\to M),$$
and, for external products as in [def-trf-external-product],
$$\Pi_{M,N}:f_XM\boxtimes f_XN\xrightarrow{\alpha_{p_1}\otimes\alpha_{p_2}}f_{X\times X}p_1^*M\otimes f_{X\times X}p_2^*N\xrightarrow{t_{X\times X}}f_{X\times X}(M\boxtimes N).$$
These definitions prescribe maps; they do not assert trace compatibility.
